**By CNN Entertainment Staff**

**(CNN) —** In the hours following the shocking death of Michael Jackson, as a stunned world struggled to process the loss of the King of Pop, one voice rose above the global chorus of grief with a chilling, deeply personal revelation. 

Lisa Marie Presley, Jackson’s former wife and the daughter of rock 'n' roll icon Elvis Presley, broke her silence in a raw, emotional blog post titled "He Knew." 

Writing on her official MySpace page late Friday, Presley detailed not only her deep sorrow over Jackson’s sudden passing at age 50, but also revealed a haunting conversation from their past—one in which Jackson accurately predicted he would meet the same tragic, premature end as her famous father.

### A Haunting Prediction

Presley recalled a conversation she had with Jackson years ago during their marriage, while discussing the 1977 death of Elvis Presley, who died of heart failure linked to prescription drug abuse at the age of 42.

"Years ago Michael and I were having a deep conversation about life in general," Presley wrote. "I can't recall the exact subject matter, but he may have been asking me about the circumstances of my father's death. At some point he turned and looked at me deep in the eyes and he stated with a calm certainty, 'I am afraid that I am going to end up like him, the way he did.'"

Presley wrote that she desperately tried to wave off the thought, but Jackson remained firm. 

"I promptly tried to deter him from the idea, at which point he just shrugged his shoulders and nodded matter-of-factly as if to let me know that he knew what he knew and that was that," she recalled. 

Fourteen years later, Jackson’s words would prove tragically prophetic. On Thursday, June 25, 2009, Jackson was pronounced dead at a Los Angeles hospital after suffering cardiac arrest, under circumstances that have drawn immediate, grim comparisons to the death of the King of Rock 'n' Roll.

"As I sit here overwhelmed with sadness, reflection, and confusion at what was my biggest failure to date... I am watching the news coverage, the speculation, the circus," Presley wrote. "I sat here with tears drying... as I am staring at this exact scenario true to form happening now, just as he predicted."

### 'Our relationship was not a sham'

Jackson and Presley surprised the world when they married in May 1994, less than a year after Jackson was hit with his first round of child sexual abuse allegations—charges he vehemently denied and settled out of court. 

At the time, critics and media commentators dismissed the union as a calculated publicity stunt designed to rehabilitate Jackson’s tarnished public image. Presley filed for divorce in January 1996, after just 18 months of marriage, feeding into the public narrative that the relationship was hollow.

In her post, however, Presley passionately defended the authenticity of their bond, pushing back against decades of media skepticism.

"Our relationship was not 'a sham' as is being reported in the press," Presley asserted. "It was an unusual relationship where two unusual people who did not live or know a 'normal life' found a connection... I do believe he loved me as much as he could love anyone, and I loved him very much."

Presley described a deeply passionate, albeit volatile, romance between two world-famous heirs to musical royalty who shared a unique understanding of intense isolation. 

### Trying to 'Save' the King of Pop

Addressing why the marriage ultimately collapsed, Presley wrote that she was overwhelmed by the destructive forces surrounding Jackson, including his burgeoning dependence on prescription medication and the "enablers" who populated his inner circle.

Drawing a agonizing parallel between her childhood spent watching her father deteriorate and her adult life with Jackson, Presley revealed that she tried desperately to save the Pop superstar from himself.

"I wanted to save him from the inevitable, which is what has just happened," she wrote. "His family and his loved ones also wanted to save him from this, but didn’t know how, and this was 14 years ago. We all worried that this would be the outcome then."

Presley explained that the emotional toll of trying to rescue Jackson eventually became unsustainable, forcing her to make a painful choice between her own well-being and his.

"I became very ill and emotionally/spiritually exhausted in my quest to save him from certain self-destructive behavior and from the awful vampires and leeches that he would inevitably attract," she admitted. "I was in over my head."

When faced with an ultimatum, she said Jackson ultimately pushed her away. "He had to make a decision. Was it the drugs and the vampires or me? And he pushed me away."

Despite their divorce and years of estrangement, Presley expressed profound guilt over whether she could have done more to intervene in Jackson's life before his sudden death. 

"The person I failed to help is being transferred to the LA County Coroners office for his Autopsy," Presley wrote. "All of my indifference and detachment that I had worked so hard to achieve over the years has just gone into the bowels of hell, and right now I am gutted."

Presley concluded her post with a heart-wrenching plea for Jackson’s soul to finally find the peace that eluded him in life.

"I desperately hope that he can be relieved from his pain, pressure, and turmoil now," she wrote. "He deserved to be freed from all of that and I hope he is in a better place, or will be."

Reflecting one final time on Jackson's eerie prediction about his own fate, Presley added a sobering postscript: "He knew."
